registered: 2026-10-14, before any Jump data was obtained or any result seen
why: Owner (2026-10-14): TTI seems to read the Jump indices well and its Jump signals have been somewhat profitable; check, and say whether that was factored in. It was not: every TTI replay so far ran on EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY and XAUUSD (HistData); Market Lab has not yet measured any Jump index.

tti_jump_specifics.assetIntel: 'Jump recent': +0.25 to the confluence score when any of the last 5 M5 bars has a range above 3 x ATR14
tti_jump_specifics.bosThr: break-of-structure threshold 0.15% of price for Jump (0.10% for other synthetics)
tti_jump_specifics.throttle: at most one Jump signal per 12 minutes per index
tti_jump_specifics.style: Jump trades as dayTrade (WATCH 2 h, READY 1 h, FIRE 1 h), not scalp

data: Deriv M1 candles for JD10, JD25, JD50, JD75, JD100 (the feed TTI itself uses), the most recent N days (default 90), downloaded by the owner with jump-history.html and converted by deriv2m1.mjs

variants.TTI43a: replay.mjs --fix F1,F2,F3 (the defect fixes of v43_prereg.json)
variants.control: TTI 4.2 on a random walk with each index's own 1-minute volatility (replay.mjs --walk 1)

measure: evaluate.mjs: plan A (TTI's own target and stop) after TTI's spread, from the signal price; R per trade, win rate, profit factor; P(win) calibration; by index
split: first half and second half of the downloaded period, by time
pass: a variant passes if, with plan A, the net average R pooled over the five Jump indices is positive with t >= 2 in the first half AND in the second half. The control must not pass; if it does, the measurement is suspect and nothing is concluded.
secondary: the owner's own TTI track record (Track Record -> export CSV, tti-track-record-*.csv): Jump rows summarised as recorded and recomputed from entry/exit; descriptive only (at most the last 100 signals; TTI's outcome tracker samples every 30 s)
unchanged: TTI's code is loaded from the owner's HTML unmodified; replay.mjs is used as committed; evaluate.mjs gains only the Jump spreads above and SPLIT=<epoch> to report the two halves (the midpoint of the downloaded period) instead of calendar years, and SPREAD_<KEY> to price a trade at the broker's spread
costs: TTI's defSpread (above) AND, separately, the spread the owner's broker quotes for each Jump index (Market Lab LAB MEASURED line or the cTrader symbol panel), via SPREAD_<KEY>. TTI's own Jump spreads are about 0.00R per trade, likely far below Deriv's; the pass rule applies at the broker's spread when it is known.
